cues.en: Wow, is it working? OK. It's amazing to see so many people show up for this talk. I've done a few talks before in conferences, and mostly people have to choose between two rooms, and they never choose mine. So this is very good. I hope you enjoyed some of the food. I'm afraid it's not enough. We didn't really expect so many people to show up. So let me try to make it up by giving you a good presentation.
cues.zh: 哇，麦克风好使吗？好的。看到这么多人来听这场演讲真是太棒了。我之前在一些大会上做过几次演讲，通常大家得在两个会场之间选，而他们从来不选我这间。所以今天能来这么多人真好。希望大家喜欢这里的点心。恐怕有点不太够，我们真没想到会来这么多人。那我今天就好好讲，争取给大家补偿回来。

cues.en: It's called 2.0 because I did this presentation in a different form some years ago in Holland. And I think none of you were there. So it's all new to you. But I did update it with some new stuff. So hopefully it will be interesting. There's a big crowd now, so I'll try to answer questions near the end. But if there's something that you don't understand on the slides or something like that, just shout.
cues.zh: 标题叫 2.0，是因为几年前我在荷兰做过一次类似形式的演讲。我想你们应该都没去过，所以对大家来说都是全新的内容。不过我也更新了一些新东西，希望会很有意思。现在台下人很多，所以答疑环节我尽量留到最后。不过如果幻灯片上有什么看不懂的地方，尽管当场喊出来。

cues.en: OK, let's get started. So text editing, that's what we're talking about. I think we all know the problem that we're working with text the whole day, with email, whatever you're working on with log files, HTML, documentation, et cetera, et cetera. If I look at myself, I spent most of my day editing text. If I'm not working on Vim, then it's email or something else.
cues.zh: 好了，我们开始吧。今天的主题是文本编辑。我想大家都有同感，我们整天都在跟文本打交道，处理邮件，或者看各种日志文件、HTML、文档等等。拿我自己来说，我一整天大部分时间都在编辑文本。如果不写 Vim，就是在回邮件或处理别的事情。

cues.en: It takes an awful lot of time. So if we can improve our text editing skills a little bit, that helps a lot. We can get more work done. Mostly when I'm not working on text editing, then mostly I'm doing meetings or stuff like that. So maybe somebody can do a presentation on how to do effective meetings. That would help. So I'm going to try to explain to you how to get more work done in less time.
cues.zh: 这非常耗费时间。所以如果我们能稍微提高一点文本编辑技能，就会有很大帮助，能完成更多工作。平时我不编辑文本的时候，大多是在开会之类的。所以或许有人能做个关于“如何高效开会”的分享，那肯定很有用。接下来我会尽量向大家介绍，如何用更少的时间完成更多的工作。

cues.en: So if you're paid by the hour, you can leave now. Of course, I'm using Vim for all the examples. That doesn't mean that I think that Vim is the only text editor that you can use or should use. As a basic rule, if you have a text editor that's good, that can do everything you need, has enough features, it does the work, and you can still expand it to do the work you expect it to do, then just stick to it.
cues.zh: 所以如果是按小时计薪的，现在可以退场了。当然，我所有的示例都会用 Vim。但这并不意味着我认为 Vim 是大家唯一可用或该用的文本编辑器。基本原则是：如果你已经有一款顺手的文本编辑器，能满足你的一切需求，功能够用、能搞定工作，而且还能扩展它来满足你的预期，那就一直用它就好。

cues.en: I mean, why learn another editor when you already have all the scales in the one you're using? So if you're using Emacs, you're happy with it. I'm not going to tell you to leave it alone, unless maybe you think it's not good. Also, I sometimes see people, even software developers, using Notepad or a similar editor. I mean, that's terrible. I mean, you're wasting a lot of time. So basically, you either use the editor that you have that you're happy with, or you switch to Vim.
cues.zh: 我是说，既然你已经熟练掌握了现有的编辑器，为什么还要去学另一个呢？所以如果你在用 Emacs 并且觉得挺好，我绝不会劝你放弃它，除非你自己觉得它不好用。另外，我有时会看到有人，甚至是软件开发者，还在用 Notepad 或类似的编辑器。这简直太糟糕了，纯粹是在浪费大把时间。所以基本上，要么用你现在用着顺手的编辑器，要么就换到 Vim。

cues.en: There's no other rule. So otherwise, I'm not going to discuss which editor is best. That's another discussion, and not very interesting. I think most of the people here are using film anyway. Oh, let me ask that. How many people of you are actually mostly using Emacs? OK. We will try to convert some people today. I won't ask how many people are using film, because then it's all hands up. So let's not do that.
cues.zh: 没有别的原则了。所以此外我不想争论哪个编辑器最好，那是另一个话题，而且也没什么意思。我想在座的大多数人本来也都是在用 Vim 的。噢，让我问一下：你们当中平时主要用 Emacs 的有多少人？好的，今天我们争取转化几个人过来。我就不问有多少人用 Vim 了，因为肯定所有人都会举手，那就不问了。

cues.en: OK, how are we going to explain these habits that I was talking about in the title? The first step, the very important step is, well, all three are important. The first step is how to know that you're doing something inefficiently. Mostly that's when you're repeating the same thing over and over and over again. And you think, well, there must be a quicker way to do this. There must be a smarter way to do this.
cues.zh: 好，我们怎么解释标题里说的那些习惯呢？第一步，非常重要的一步是——其实三步都很重要。第一步是，如何知道自己正在低效地做事。通常就是你在一遍又一遍地重复同一件事。然后你想，嗯，肯定有更快的办法，肯定有更聪明的办法。

cues.en: For example, what I do myself quite often is you have a function name, somebody reviews your change, says, ah, this is a terrible function name. Use another name. So you have to go all over your code and change one name into another. Well, obviously, if you're going to find the name, type the same name over and over again, then not only is it not efficient, you're also going to make mistakes that you have to fix later. And it's even getting more complicated, like if you have five names that you have to change into five different names.
cues.zh: 比如，我自己经常遇到的是，你有个函数名，别人审查你的改动时说，啊，这个函数名太糟了，换个名字。于是你得翻遍代码，把一个名字改成另一个。显然，如果你要查找这个名字，一遍遍输入同一个名字，那不仅低效，还会犯错，之后还得修。更复杂的是，比如你有五个名字要改成五个不同的名字。

cues.en: And there's a pattern in how you change them. And obviously, you don't want to type that. You want to find some way to do it quickly. The trick here is that you have to do this while you are working. So every time you're working on something, you have to kind of look back like, what did I do the last five minutes? Did I repeat myself? Can I do this in a quicker way? So you have to detect your inefficiency. That's actually quite tricky. But I'm going to give examples, of course.
cues.zh: 而且你改它们的方式是有规律的。显然，你不想手动输入这些。你想找到某种快速完成的方法。诀窍在于，你必须在工作过程中做这件事。所以每次做某件事时，你得回头看看：过去五分钟我做了什么？我是不是在重复？我能不能更快地做？所以你得发现自己的低效。这其实挺难的。不过我当然会举例。

cues.en: Well, find a quicker way. Well, every good editor has ways to do things quickly. The trick is, how do you find them? You don't want to spend the whole day to find a better solution. You want to find it in five minutes. So I'm going to give you some ideas of how to find better ways, quicker ways. And the last and also important is how to make it a habit.
cues.zh: 好，找到更快的办法。每个好编辑器都有快速做事的方法。诀窍是，你怎么找到它们？你不想花一整天去找一个更好的方案，你想在五分钟内找到。所以我会给你一些思路，告诉你如何找到更好的、更快的办法。最后一点也很重要，就是如何把它变成习惯。

cues.en: the whole reference manual of Vim. But that doesn't mean you know the commands. You don't really use them. So you have to make it a habit to actually use them. Otherwise, you have to think about every key that you type. And you really want to get the commands in your fingers done automatically. So it must be a habit. So basically, what you need to do is you have to see the problem. You have to find a solution and make it a habit. That's quite simple, isn't it?
cues.zh: 整本 Vim 参考手册。但这不代表你掌握这些命令。你并不会真正去用它们。所以你必须养成实际使用它们的习惯。否则，你每敲一个键都得想一想。你真正想要的是让命令自动地从手指间敲出来。所以它必须成为习惯。基本上，你需要做的就是：发现问题，找到解决方案，并把它变成习惯。很简单，对吧？

cues.en: That's gone. About the title, why seven habits? Why not three or why not 42? Well, actually 42 will be a different book. I saw this book and I read it. And I think it's quite an interesting book and gives you a lot of tips about work and life and family and all kinds of things. And I can recommend it for normal reading. And I also like the title.
cues.zh: 那个先不说了。关于标题，为什么是七个习惯？为什么不是三个，或者为什么不是 42？其实 42 会是另一本书。我看到这本书并读了它。我觉得它挺有意思，给了你很多关于工作、生活、家庭等各种事情的技巧。我可以推荐它作为普通读物。而且我也喜欢这个标题。

cues.en: So I made a title for this presentation, a variant on this title. Of course, there's also another variant on this title, Seven Years of Highly Defective People. I just love Dilbert. This is really a great book that explains a bit about the characters around Dilbert and why they are drawn, the way they are drawn, and how they developed over the first seven years. That's really a nice book, especially if you like Dilbert, of course.
cues.zh: 我给这个演讲起了个标题，是这个标题的一个变体。当然，这个标题还有另一个变体：《七年高度缺陷人士》。我就是喜欢 Dilbert。这真是本好书，它讲了一点 Dilbert 周围角色的情况，以及他们为什么被画成那样、前七年里是怎么发展的。这书真不错，当然，前提是你喜欢 Dilbert。

cues.en: OK, let's go along with the first habit. This is something simple to start with. So you have this code, and you're wondering, where is this variable used? I used RXE for an example. So what you do, you search for the name, and you keep pressing N to find all the occurrences of that variable. And then you search for another variable and do the same thing again. You browse through the whole code, and then you type.
cues.zh: 好，我们先从第一个习惯说起。这个很简单，适合开头。你有这段代码，然后想知道这个变量在哪儿用到？我用了 RXE 作例子。那你要做的就是搜索这个名字，然后不停按 N 来找到这个变量的所有出现位置。接着再搜另一个变量，再做一遍。你浏览完整个代码，然后输入。

cues.en: a long name. But if you look closely, you can see there's a typo in there, so you don't find anything. Well, this is what happens a lot if you don't know the commands of your editor. So you keep typing a lot of text, typing a lot of commands, and wasting a lot of time, obviously. So what's a quicker way? Well, what's important here? How do you find a quicker way? In this example, I will say that
cues.zh: 一个很长的名字。但仔细看，你会发现里面有个拼写错误，所以你什么也找不到。如果你不熟悉编辑器的命令，这种情况经常发生。于是你不停输入大量文本、输入大量命令，显然浪费了很多时间。那更快的办法是什么？这里重要的是什么？你怎么找到更快的办法？在这个例子里，我会说

cues.en: You just search in the help for Vim, and you find something about search highlighting. And you think, well, I'm searching. I want to see what's going on, so highlighting will help. And so you turn on the highlight search option. Of course, you need to search a little bit in the help to find this. And especially the star command. Well, I think most people that actually use Vim know about the star command, especially if you looked on the website. I think it's actually the first tip.
cues.zh: 你只是在 Vim 的帮助里搜索，找到关于搜索高亮的内容。然后你想，嗯，我在搜索，我想看清发生了什么，所以高亮会有帮助。于是你打开搜索高亮选项。当然，你得在帮助里搜一会儿才能找到这个。尤其是星号命令。嗯，我觉得大多数真正用 Vim 的人都知道星号命令，尤其是如果你看过网站。我觉得这其实是最早的技巧之一。

cues.en: one of the first tips. Well, obviously, what you then get is that you get all the things you were looking for highlighted. And it gives you a great overview of where a variable is used. Of course, this is just a small screen. If you have one of the bigger screens, you have a much better overview. And that works really great. Of course, the star command you use when the cursor is on a word. So you type star, and it looks for other occurrences of that word.
cues.zh: 最早技巧之一。显然，然后你会得到的是，你要找的所有内容都会被高亮出来。它让你对变量在哪儿使用有很好的全局了解。当然，这只是个小屏幕。如果你有更大的屏幕，概览会好得多。这真的很好用。当然，星号命令是在光标位于某个词上时用的。所以你输入星号，它就会查找那个词的其他出现位置。

cues.en: So how do you make this a habit? Well, the easiest is to switch on highlight search in your VMRC file, in your startup file. So it's awesome. I do that. I always have the highlight search optional. That does mean that for every search you do, you see all the matches. And that sometimes means you have a whole yellow screen. That happens. And so I added the hint here that you can switch it off.
cues.zh: 那怎么把它变成习惯？最简单的就是在你的 vimrc 文件、启动文件里打开搜索高亮。这很棒。我就这么做。我总是打开搜索高亮选项。这确实意味着你每次搜索都会看到所有匹配项。有时这意味着满屏都是黄色。这会发生。所以我在这里加了提示，你可以把它关掉。

cues.en: for a moment, and then it switched on automatically again when you search for something. Again, you have to make it habit. So just repeat that star command. You have the option switched on, so that works. And you have to use it again and again. And after a little while, you don't even think of it. You just look at a variable, you automatically press star. There's, of course, many other ways to move around quickly, just to mention one.
cues.zh: 一会儿，当你搜索别的内容时它又会自动开启。同样，你得把它变成习惯。只要反复去用那个星号（*）命令就行。只要开启了这个选项，它就会起作用。而且你得反复去用。过一阵子，你甚至想都不用想。只要看一眼变量，就会下意识地按星号键。当然，快速跳转的方法还有很多，这只是其中一种。

cues.en: Folding was added in VIM 6. Some people like it, some people don't. So you'll have to find out yourself if you like it or not. Maybe I can switch and give a life. Oh, that's working. So what I have here is just a source file. Here you see a marker in the source file with three brackets. And that actually marks an area in the code.
cues.zh: 折叠功能是在 Vim 6 中加入的。有人喜欢，有人不喜欢。所以喜不喜欢得你自己去体会。或许我可以切过去现场演示一下。噢，搞定了。我现在这里就是一个源文件。你可以看到源文件里有一个由三个括号组成的标记。它其实标记了代码中的一个区域，

cues.en: that can be folded away. So I can just click on the minus sign. If I click right, OK. And then it's closed. And if I just move around to some of the other faults, I can move in just by moving the cursor, and it opens. So you can see the code. That's quite convenient. So there's a few commands that you can use with faults to move around. So you have a nice overview of the functions in your file. And you can move around, and then move the cursor, and it's open. So you can see the code.
cues.zh: 这个区域是可以折叠起来的。我只要点击减号就行。只要点对位置，好的，它就折叠起来了。如果我移到其他折叠处，只要移动光标进去，它就会展开。这样你就能看到代码了。这非常方便。所以有一些配合折叠来进行光标跳转的命令。这样你就能对文件中的函数有一个清晰的概览。你可以四处浏览，光标移过去就会展开，从而查看代码。

cues.en: Just one of the many ways to quickly move around. OK, second example. If you're working with X Windows, you have these terrible function names that you have to use all the time. I mean, it's just impossible to type right in advance unless you're perfect, but nobody's perfect. And there's small print, there's capital prints, and there's everything. You type it wrong all the time.
cues.zh: 这只是快速跳转的众多方法之一。好，第二个例子。如果你在用 X Windows 开发，就总得去写那些又臭又长的函数名。我是说，除非你完美无瑕，否则根本不可能一次敲对，但人无完人。里面有小写、有大写，混杂在一起，你总是会拼错。

cues.en: One solution that people I've seen using is to copy paste the name. So you have a list of the names. You copy paste them. That's a little bit quicker, but still, it's a bit slow. There's a much quicker way. So how do you find this method? Well, what I often recommend is just ask around. Ask somebody, a colleague, or a friend, how do you do this? And that's actually one of the best ways to find a better way. Of course, you have to do it.
cues.zh: 我见过的解决办法之一就是复制粘贴函数名。你手头有一份名称列表，然后复制粘贴过去。这确实快了一点，但还是有点慢。其实有快得多的办法。那怎么发现这种技巧呢？我通常建议到处问问。问问同事或朋友：你们是怎么弄的？这其实是找到更好方法的最佳途径之一。当然，你得主动去问。

cues.en: Don't be shy. Ask a question. And this colleague of yours that, of course, is much better in film, then tells you use the control n command or the next insert mode completion command. And what that does is you type some of the letters. So what happens here is you type five letters, which is the start of one of the function names. Then you hit control n.
cues.zh: 别害羞，尽管提问。而你那位显然更懂 Vim 的同事就会告诉你：用 Ctrl-N 命令，也就是插入模式下的“补全下一个”命令。它的用法是只输入一部分字母。具体来说就是先敲五个字母，也就是某个函数名的开头，然后按下 Ctrl-N。

cues.en: And Finn will complete the whole word for you. Well, if you're lucky. I mean, if you look closely, you see here there's like 16 function names that start with the same five letters. So you might have to hit Control-N a few times to get to the right one. But at least that's a lot less typing and a lot less mistakes than when you would try to type it directly. This doesn't only work for strange function names, it also works for
cues.zh: 然后 Vim 就会帮你把整个词补全。呃，如果你运气好的话。仔细看的话，你会发现这里大概有 16 个函数名都以相同的五个字母开头。所以你可能得多按几次 Ctrl-N 才能选到正确的。但至少比起完全手动敲出来，这少打了很多字，也少犯很多错误。这不仅适用于古怪的函数名，同样适用于

cues.en: the name of people you're applying to in an email. I mean, if you reply to somebody and you type his name wrong, that's not very good. I mean, not very nice. So I use completion a lot, especially for people from strange countries that have these names that are really hard to type sometimes. I mean, no offense, but not everybody has English names or Dutch names. It looks very strange.
cues.zh: 你在邮件里回复的人名。我的意思是，如果你给某人回信却把名字打错了，那可不太好，显得很不礼貌。所以我经常用自动补全，特别是有些来自异国他乡的人，他们的名字有时真的很难拼。无意冒犯，但并不是所有人都叫英文名或荷兰名，有些名字看起来真的很生僻。

cues.en: In Vim 7, I discovered that often you want an overview of all the matches that exist. So I made this fantastic, high-tech menu. Doesn't it look great? And you can actually get an overview of all the matches that have been found. And you can use the cursor keys to scroll through them. So that's also for dummies who don't know exactly how Vim does this.
cues.zh: 在 Vim 7 中，我发现经常需要总览所有存在的匹配项。所以我做了这个超棒的高科技菜单。看起来不错吧？你确实可以总览所有已找到的匹配项。还能用方向键滚动浏览。所以这也适合那些不太清楚 Vim 具体怎么做的“小白”。

cues.en: And also, what this shows is it's actually only completion. And only is a term that we invented to avoid a very long name. What this does is actually it looks at the context. So it doesn't just look at the word before the cursor. It looks a bit further back. And in this case, it finds this pointer. It looks up the type of the pointer, finds out that it's a structure.
cues.zh: 另外，这也表明它其实只是补全。only 是我们为了避免名字太长而造的词。它实际做的是查看上下文。所以它不只看光标前的单词。它会再往前看一些。在这个例子里，它找到这个指针。它查出指针的类型，发现是一个结构体。

cues.en: And the structure has members. And then the members are obtained, and these are the alternatives that you get. So you don't even have to type anything here. The cursor could have pointed a silver arrow there. And you just type Control-N, and you get all the possible names that can be valid there, hopefully.
cues.zh: 这个结构体有成员。然后获取这些成员，它们就是你得到的候选项。所以你在这里甚至不用输入任何东西。光标本来可以停在那里，就像有个银色箭头指过去。你只需按 Control-N，就能得到所有在那里可能有效的名字——希望如此。

cues.en: But OmniCompletion is a complicated thing. It currently has been implemented for a few languages, like C, Python. I don't think Java really works. But it's still under development, and we could use some help. So if you know a language very well, maybe you can help developing it. It's all written in VimScript. You don't have to program C or anything. But I have to admit, it's not really easy. But with a little bit of effort, we can get it done.
cues.zh: 但 OmniCompletion 是个复杂的东西。目前只为少数语言实现了，比如 C、Python。我不认为 Java 真的能用。但它仍在开发中，我们需要一些帮助。所以如果你很熟悉某门语言，也许可以帮忙开发。它全部用 VimScript 编写。你不需要写 C 之类的。但我得承认，这并不容易。不过稍加努力，我们就能完成。

cues.en: And sorry about the ugly menu. OK, next habit. I'm not a native English speaker. I do know English quite well, I think, but I still make lots of mistakes, especially when typing. Finn now has a spell checker, which is very nice. The next slide shows that.
cues.zh: 抱歉菜单有点丑。好，下一个习惯。我不是英语母语者。我觉得自己英语还不错，但仍然会犯很多错误，尤其是打字时。Finn 现在有拼写检查器，这很不错。下一张幻灯片会展示。

cues.en: The spell checker, you can switch it on. And it will highlight, in this case, I was using the GUI version, GVIM. So it will just underline the mistakes with a nice wobbly line. And then you can go there and either use the mouse or use keyboard commands to see the alternatives for fixing that. So in this case, it's just that the first letter was wrong. This works.
cues.zh: 拼写检查器可以打开。它会高亮，这里我用的是 GUI 版本 GVIM。所以它只会用漂亮的波浪线给错误加下划线。然后你可以过去，用鼠标或键盘命令查看修正候选。所以在这个例子里，只是第一个字母错了。这很管用。

cues.en: It works quite well, especially if you have only a few mistakes in your text. And if you don't know the language very well, so you don't know the correction, this works really well. It's supported for about 30 languages. So that's quite good. But still, if you have common typing mistakes, and you have to fix every one of them in this way, that's still taking a lot of time. So you think there must be a better way, and there is.
cues.zh: 它效果很好，尤其是文本里只有少量错误时。如果你不太懂这门语言，不知道该怎么改，这会非常有用。它支持大约 30 种语言。所以相当不错。但如果有很多常见的打字错误，而且每个都得这样修，那还是很花时间。于是你会想肯定有更好的办法，确实有。

cues.en: In this example, I'm using a way to find the solution using the Maylist archives. You know the theme Maylist archive is really a treasure of all kinds of tips and suggestions and answers to questions. So if you use the right keywords, just search in the archives, and mostly you will find a solution. Actually, this one is somewhere in the archives, if you can find it. But of course, now it's on the screen, so that's a lot easier.
cues.zh: 这个例子里，我用邮件列表归档来寻找解决方案。你知道，邮件列表归档真是个宝库，里面有各种技巧、建议和问题解答。所以只要用对关键词，在归档里搜一下，大多都能找到解决办法。其实这个例子就在归档里的某个地方，如果你能找到的话。当然，现在它就在屏幕上，那就容易多了。

cues.en: What does this do? You basically take the words that you misspell. So you want to type the, but you type the. And you make an abbreviation for it, an insert of abbreviation. So that's really simple. That's one of the basic things in Vim. You just have to think about actually doing it. And then you can also, as an extra, highlight the typing mistakes. So when the correction doesn't happen for some reason, because abbreviations don't always
cues.zh: 这是做什么的？你基本上是把拼错的词拿来做处理。比如你想输入 the，却打错了。然后为它建一个缩写，也就是插入模式缩写。这其实很简单。这是 Vim 里的基础功能之一。你只需要想着真的去用它。然后，作为额外功能，你还可以高亮输入错误。这样当纠正因为某些原因没触发时——毕竟缩写并不总是

cues.en: kick in. You can also highlight them so you can have an overview. So then you get this. So you have some text. And this is something I typed and typed wrong. Actually, I had a hard time typing this because the corrections kept kicking in and correcting me. So I had to switch that off. So these are just a few examples of common typos. So you type Linux instead of Linux. And you type in ecstasy. And of course, these are words.
cues.zh: 能生效。你也可以把它们高亮出来，方便总览。然后就会得到这个。你有一些文本。这是我输入时打错的内容。其实我输入这个很费劲，因为纠正总是触发并改正我。所以我不得不把它关掉。这些只是常见错别字的一些例子。比如你把 Linux 拼错了，把 in ecstasy 也打错了。当然，这些词

cues.en: that are really wrong. You would never have them in your text. So then you can make an abbreviation. Some words are just, you still typed them wrong, but they're also valid words. So then you'll have to decide yourself if you want to correct them or not. The nice thing about this is it's really fast. I mean, you just continue typing all your mistakes, and it corrects them for you automatically. The only thing is you have to make a list. I have made a list for myself, because I always make the same mistakes over and over again.
cues.zh: 错得很离谱。你的文本里根本不会出现这些词。那就可以给它们建缩写。有些词呢，你虽然打错了，但它们本身也是合法单词。那你就得自己决定要不要纠正。这个功能的好处是很快。我的意思是，你就继续把错误都打出来，它会自动帮你纠正。唯一的问题是，你得维护一个列表。我给自己做了一个列表，因为我总是反复犯同样的错误。

cues.en: And you probably make different mistakes, depending on your keyboard and what you're used to. So you'll have to make your own list. And if you want to make this a habit, one thing you need to do is if you notice you make certain typing mistakes, you have to add that word to the list and find the correction. And of course, for more advanced users, you can make a mapping to actually do that. So you don't have to manually edit that list, but you can do it automatically.
cues.zh: 你可能会根据键盘和习惯犯不同的错误。所以你得做自己的列表。如果你想养成习惯，有一件事必须做：当你注意到自己犯了某些输入错误时，就把那个词加到列表里，并找到对应的纠正。当然，对更高级的用户，你可以做一个映射来自动完成这件事。这样就不用手动编辑列表，而是可以自动完成。

cues.en: OK. Well, when I started working for Google, I found this whole pack of codes. That's fantastic, but quite difficult to understand. So you have to somehow find a way to maneuver between all the files, find out how it works. And that's quite difficult if it's a lot of codes. Of course, this inefficiency is very easy to detect. You just can't find your way.
cues.zh: 好。嗯，当我开始在 Google 工作时，我发现这里有整整一大堆代码。很厉害，但也很难理解。所以你得想办法在所有这些文件之间穿梭，弄清楚它是怎么运作的。如果代码很多，这就相当困难。当然，这种低效很容易被发现。你就是找不到方向。

cues.en: The solution is a bit more difficult. In this case, I give the example of you look in the film quick reference. Of course, there's also the user manual, which is very useful. You just search around in some of the pages on the film help. And the quick reference is very good because it's compact. I have some keywords, so if you look for the right keywords, you can find a hint about what you're looking for. So for moving around in files, I have two examples here.
cues.zh: 解决方案稍微复杂一点。举个例子，你可以查阅 Vim 快速参考。当然还有用户手册，也非常有用。你只要在 Vim 帮助页里搜搜看就行。快速参考非常好，因为它很紧凑。里面有一些关键词，所以如果你找对了关键词，就能找到所需内容的线索。关于在文件间跳转，我这里有两个例子。

cues.en: One of them is using the C tags program. I'm wondering, how many of you know C tags? OK, quite a few, but not everybody. Of course, C tags generate a tags file. What I mostly do is if I find new code, I generate a tags file. And I do it like this, with the dash r, which means recursive, and with the dot, which means the current directory. So basically, you.
cues.zh: 其中一个是使用 ctags 程序。我想知道，你们有多少人了解 ctags？好的，不少，但不是所有人。当然，ctags 会生成一个 tags 文件。我通常的做法是，拿到新代码后，就生成一个 tags 文件。就像这样操作，加上 -r 参数表示递归，加上点号表示当前目录。所以基本上，你……

cues.en: You have to move to the right directory and say, generate a text file for everything below this, the whole directory tree. Don't do that for a big tree, because it will take too long. But normally, for libraries and stuff like that, it works just fine. Then you can use the tag command to jump to a tag. And you use tnext if you have multiple matches, which especially happens in C++ code. There must be.
cues.zh: 你需要切到正确的目录，然后生成其下所有内容、整个目录树的 tags 文件。如果目录树很大就别这么做，因为耗时太长了。但通常对于代码库之类的，它运行得很好。然后你就可以用 tag 命令跳转到标签。如果有多个匹配项，可以用 tnext，这在 C++ 代码中尤为常见。肯定会有……

cues.en: lots of matches for the same word. You can move around or use tselect, which is another tags command. There's lots of tags commands. You can just look it up in the help file. The important thing here is that tags only finds where things are defined. So where a variable is defined or where a function is defined and a few other things. But it doesn't find where they are used. So if you have a function and you want to know where is this function invoked from, you have to do something else.
cues.zh: 同一个词往往有很多匹配项。你可以来回切换，或者用 tselect，那是另一个 tags 命令。还有很多 tags 命令，直接查阅帮助文件即可。这里重要的是，tags 只能找到定义的所在位置。比如变量在哪里定义、函数在哪里定义等等。但它找不到它们在哪里被使用。所以如果你有一个函数，想知道它是从哪里被调用的，就得另寻他法了。

cues.en: There's C-scope. And that's not a very well-known tool. Within Google, we have other things that know where matches are to be found. But a very common way is to use grep. And if you look closely, you can see there's no exclamation mark here. So this is not the external grep. This is the internal grep, which was added in VIM7.
cues.zh: 可以用 cscope。不过这个工具不太出名。在 Google 内部，我们有其他工具来查找匹配位置。但一种非常普遍的做法是使用 grep。如果你仔细看，会发现这里没有感叹号。所以这不是外部的 grep，而是 Vim 7 中新增的内置 grep。

cues.en: Vim knows about compressed files. It accepts this wildcard, which means search in a whole directory tree. So there's a few tricks that it can do better than the normal grep command. But it's slower. So if you have a lot of files, you might still want to use the original grep. And lightmake will just invoke it, get the list, and then use that. So that's up to you. Anyway.
cues.zh: Vim 能够识别压缩文件。它支持这种通配符，表示在整个目录树中搜索。因此比起普通的 grep 命令，它有一些更厉害的招数。但它的速度更慢。所以如果有大量文件，你可能还是想用原本的 grep。lightmake 会直接调用它，获取列表并使用。所以这取决于你。总之……

cues.en: You get a long list of matches, and then you have to move through the matches. If there's a few matches, you can just use C next and C list and other C commands to manipulate the list. And there's one nice thing, though, that if you have a lot of matches or you want to get a no view, you have the quick fish window. So you use the colon C open command. You get the quick fish window. And there you can actually search around. It's just a normal text window.
cues.zh: 你会得到一长串匹配项列表，接着需要在匹配项之间移动。如果匹配项不多，直接用 cnext、clist 等 c 开头的命令来操作列表就行。不过还有个很棒的功能：如果匹配项很多，或者你想看个全局概览，可以使用 quickfix 窗口。输入 :copen 命令，就会打开 quickfix 窗口。在那里你就可以随意搜索，它就是一个普通的文本窗口。

cues.en: except that when you hit Enter, you jump to the position that's mentioned there. OK. Well, of course, there's many other ways to move around. And since it's quite important, I thought I'd make another slide about it. Well, go to File, GF. You can just type that on any file name, and it will jump to that file, if it can find it, of course. The nice thing, it even works on hypertext links.
cues.zh: 只不过按 Enter 时，会跳到那里提到的位置。好。当然，还有很多其他移动方式。因为这很重要，我想再专门做一页幻灯片。好，用 gf 跳到文件。你只要在任意文件名上输入它，它就会跳到那个文件——当然，前提是能找到。妙的是，它甚至对超文本链接也有效。

cues.en: RW plug-in that does that for you. And most people don't know that, but it actually works. Of course, you'd see the HTML as HTML. You don't see it rendered. But still, it's very nice. An important thing is that the path option should be set correctly. Because that's how Vim knows where to find your files. And they could be anywhere, so you have to make sure it's set OK.
cues.zh: 有 RW 插件可以帮你做到这一点。多数人不知道，但它确实能用。当然，你会看到 HTML 源码，而不是渲染后的效果。但依然很不错。重要的是 path 选项要设置正确。因为 Vim 靠它知道去哪里找你的文件。文件可能在任何地方，所以一定要确保设置好。

cues.en: There's a few more commands. Actually, the square brackets i, that's a capital I, searches in include files. So that's very useful if you have a lot of library functions that you're using and you don't know exactly how they're defined or you can't find the documentation. You can search in the header file, the include files, and again, if path is set correctly.
cues.zh: 还有几个命令。其实，方括号 i，也就是大写 I，会在 include 文件中搜索。所以如果你用了很多库函数，又不清楚它们具体怎么定义，或者找不到文档，这就很有用。你可以在头文件、include 文件中搜索——同样，前提是 path 设置正确。

cues.en: I quite often just use the square bracket tab and just jump to the first match, basically. And hopefully that's the right one. And that's very quick. Unless you have a lot of include file, then it's slow. I think I forgot making that into a habit. Anyway, you can do that yourself. Let's work together. There's a lot of programs, especially about layout, email.
cues.zh: 我经常就用方括号 Tab，直接跳到第一个匹配项。希望那就是对的。这非常快。除非 include 文件很多，那就慢了。我想我还没养成这个习惯。总之，你可以自己这样做。我们一起努力吧。有很多程序，尤其是排版、邮件相关的。

cues.en: Lots of stuff that basically work with text, but add something to it, like layout or some format, like in a spreadsheet. The problem is that those editors are OK, but it's sometimes so difficult to type a lot of text. And the WQ appearing in your text is not very nice. So that's one of the inefficient things. And sometimes when I have to
cues.zh: 很多东西本质上处理文本，但会给它加上些东西，比如排版或某种格式，像电子表格那样。问题是这些编辑器还行，但有时输入大量文本很困难。而且文本里冒出 WQ 也不好看。这就是低效之处之一。有时当我不得不——

cues.en: I write a document with markup and it has to look nice, then what I mostly do is something that you have to find out about. Of course, again, the trick is, how do you find out how to do this? Well, in this case, I give the example, ask on the Vimeo list. There's lots of people on the Vimeo list that are excellent in giving very nice answers to your questions and very patiently and understanding that you don't know everything. And it's actually amazing that there's a few people that
cues.zh: 我用标记语言写文档，而且它得看起来不错时，我主要做的是你得自己去了解的东西。当然，诀窍还是：你怎么弄清该怎么做？在这种情况下，我举个例子：去 Vim 邮件列表提问。列表里有很多人非常擅长回答你的问题，很有耐心，也理解你不可能什么都知道。而且实际上很神奇的是，有几个人……

cues.en: seem to be doing nothing the whole day but answering questions on the VIM mail list. And I'm so glad, because otherwise I would have to do that, and I just simply don't have the time. So let me thank all the people on the VIM mail list that answered the questions there. That's just great. So you ask this question, and then somebody says, oh, just type your text in VIM if you like it. With just a trick, you switch off automatic text wrapping.
cues.zh: 似乎整天什么都不干，只是在 Vim 邮件列表上回答问题。我太高兴了，因为否则就得我来做，而我真的没时间。所以让我感谢 Vim 邮件列表上所有回答问题的人。太棒了。你问这个问题，然后有人说：哦，如果你喜欢，就直接在 Vim 里输入文本。只要一个小技巧，关掉自动换行。

cues.en: if it was on anyway. You switch on the rep, so the lines rep. And you switch on line break. This is, of course, the essential part of it. That means that the lines are wrapped at blank spaces or special characters. So the words are not broken halfway, so it's much more easy to read. It's just a simple trick. But actually, if you do this, you can have paragraphs of one line that you can copy paste between your word or
cues.zh: 反正它本来就开着。你打开 wrap，行就会换行。再打开 linebreak。当然，这是其中的关键部分。这意味着行会在空白处或特殊字符处折行。所以单词不会被从中间断开，读起来就容易多了。就是个简单的小技巧。但其实，这么做的话，你可以让一段就是一行，方便在 Word 或

cues.en: OpenOffice or whatever, and Vim. So you can edit them in Vim and copy them back. And that works quite well. Of course, it still works to do the copying back and forth. But it's at least a lot better than trying to type your text in Word. Of course, there's one catch. You can't copy paste the formatting. So if you have bold stuff and underlining, that will be gone. It's not perfect.
cues.zh: OpenOffice 之类的，还有 Vim 之间复制粘贴。这样你就可以在 Vim 里编辑，再复制回去。这招相当好用。当然，来回复制也仍然可行。但至少比在 Word 里硬敲文本好多了。当然，有个问题。格式没法复制粘贴。所以如果有加粗和下划线，那些都会丢失。并不完美。

cues.en: Yeah, there's other ways to do this, like removing the, doesn't say that. There's another way is that when you copy and paste text, you can actually insert line breaks and remove them again. But I'll leave that to you to find out how to do that. Yeah, that's the problem. It still exists. I actually have to scan documents that I write if I don't leave something in there. OK.
cues.zh: 对，还有别的办法，比如去掉……这个就不细说了。还有一种办法是，复制粘贴文本时，你可以插入换行，然后再把它们删掉。但具体怎么做，我留给你自己发现。对，这就是问题所在。它仍然存在。如果我不在里面留点东西，我其实得扫描我自己写的文档。好。

cues.en: Just one more example that I was thinking of. This is actually something I do when I release a new version of Vim or make a few patches, is I have to check if there's nothing wrong on some kind of system. And the compiler doesn't run for every arrow. So what I do is I run the Vim source code through lint. It still exists. And I do that actually with like 20 different combinations of features.
cues.zh: 再举一个我想到的例子。这其实是我发布 Vim 新版本或打几个补丁时会做的事：我得检查在某些系统上有没有问题。编译器不会针对每个架构都跑一遍。所以我会用 lint 跑一遍 Vim 源码。它还在。而且我实际上会跑大约 20 种不同的特性组合。

cues.en: What I get is an awful long list with all kinds of warnings. And most of these warnings are for header files, so I can't fix them. I mean, well, I could perhaps edit the header file to fix the problem there, but that's a lot of work. And then if you go from GTK 2.1.3 to the next version, then it's all gone again. They're mostly GTK warnings, I'm afraid.
cues.zh: 我得到的是长长一大串各种警告。其中大多数警告都来自头文件，所以我修不了。我的意思是，也许我可以编辑头文件来修复那里的问题，但那工作量很大。而且如果你从 GTK 2.1.3 换到下一个版本，它们又全没了。恐怕它们大多是 GTK 的警告。

cues.en: So you have this long list of warnings, and it's very difficult to find the errors that you are actually looking for. So how do you do that? Well, quite simple, actually. This time you just think, OK, I can do it myself. So you don't ask anyone. You don't look on the mail. You just do it. And you write this simple function, which is nothing but a global command that searches for the things you don't want to see and deletes them. Of course, the trick here is to make the pattern.
cues.zh: 所以你拿到这一长串警告，很难从中找到你真正想找的错误。那怎么办呢？其实很简单。这次你就想，好吧，我自己能搞定。于是你不问别人。你不去查邮件列表。你直接动手。你写一个简单的函数，它不过是一个全局命令，用来搜索你不想看到的东西并删掉它们。当然，这里的诀窍在于让模式

cues.en: match the lines you want to delete and not match any lines you want to keep. So you have to think about that yourself. In this case, I do things like look for GTK and enum something, and then I don't have that in my code, so it must be in a header file. And the Perl stuff gives errors that match this, so they're all gone, and then it cleans up. Then I make a mapping for this and the score CL.
cues.zh: 匹配你想删除的行，同时不匹配任何你想保留的行。所以这得你自己想清楚。在这个例子里，我会做类似查找 GTK 和 enum 某个东西的操作，而我的代码里没有这些，所以它一定在头文件里。Perl 相关的东西会给出符合这个模式的错误，于是它们全被清掉，然后就干净了。然后我给这个功能做个映射，再 source 到命令行。

cues.en: I have a lot of mappings that start with an underscore, because underscore actually is an original VI command. It's not properly documented, but it is a command. But you don't never use it. So you can actually use it for mappings without interfering with blocking one of the theme commands. So that's a very good thing for more advanced mappings. So you call your function. And of course, this is to signal the entering the

cues.en: So that means Vim knows that this is another pointer. And actually, you can see it's a pointer to this type. 我用那个。

cues.en: very much enjoy using open source. I very much enjoy writing open source. It's just a lot of fun. I think Linus used that as his main remark on what he thinks about Linux. It's a lot of fun. And I think most people agree that open source is a lot of fun for everybody. The problem is people have to make money. If you make something open source, then making money from it is difficult. It's not impossible. It's just difficult.
cues.zh: 我非常喜欢使用开源，也很喜欢编写开源。这纯粹是乐趣无穷。我想 Linus 在评价 Linux 时主要也是这么说的：太好玩了。而且我想大多数人都会同意，开源对大家来说都充满了乐趣。但问题是人总得赚钱。如果你把软件开源了，想靠它赚钱就会很困难。倒不是不可能，只是很难。

cues.en: I actually had another presentation on that a couple of years ago, how to make money with open source software. And if you see the overview, you realize that there's just small parts of open source that you can make money with. So the result is, yes, we have closed source because people want to make money with software. And I think the Mac is another example of where Apple thought, well, we like to give it away, but we also have to make money somehow.
cues.zh: 几年前我其实就此做过另一场演讲，讲如何靠开源软件赚钱。如果你看下整体情况，就会发现开源中能赚钱的其实只有极小一部分。所以结果就是，没错，我们有了闭源软件，因为大家想靠软件盈利。我觉得 Mac 也是另一个例子，Apple 也会觉得，虽然我们很想免费送，但无论如何也得想办法赚钱。

cues.en: So they have to close some parts, but they actually have given away a lot of their stuff. But there's a gray area somewhere about what you can give away and what you can't give away. Google has the same problem. I mean, most people in Google think, let's just give it away. I mean, we make such great software. Let's just give it to everybody. But our shareholders don't agree. And we have a whole open source team within Google.
cues.zh: 所以他们不得不闭源某些部分，但其实他们也免费开放了很多东西。不过在哪些可以开放、哪些不能开放之间，存在一片灰色地带。Google 也面临同样的问题。我的意思是，Google 大多数人都会觉得，直接开源送给大家吧。我们写出了这么棒的软件，就免费分享给所有人吧。但我们的股东不同意。我们在 Google 内部专门有一个开源团队，

cues.en: who are actively looking into all the parts of software that we have and find out can we publish this, can we give this away, or do we need to keep it a secret? Because that's the choice that we have to make. That's tough. For me, I think it's OK to use closed source software, but I keep promoting open source. I think that's the best way to approach this. OK? Another question? Yes?
cues.zh: 他们一直在积极审查我们现有的所有软件部分，看看我们到底能不能发布这个、能不能送出去，还是必须得保密？因为这是我们必须做的抉择。这挺难的。对我来说，我觉得使用闭源软件没什么问题，但我会坚持推广开源。我认为这是最好的应对方式。好了，还有别的问题吗？请讲？

cues.en: plug-ins for GUI editors kind of things. Yeah, as I said in one of the examples is copy-paste works, but it's not very nice. Eclipse is, I think, the application where it's asked most often. Eclipse has its own editor, and it's quite good, but it's not thin.
cues.zh: 比如 GUI 编辑器的插件之类的。对，就像我刚才举的一个例子，复制粘贴虽然可行，但体验并不好。我想 Eclipse 是大家问得最多的应用了。Eclipse 有自己的编辑器，而且相当不错，但它并不轻巧。

cues.en: So people that are used to all the VIMP commands have the big set of all functions and scripts that are written. They can't use them inside Eclipse, so that's a problem. The main problem with Eclipse is that they defined an editor interface. So you can actually plug in another editor. But that interface is so complicated, it's actually just made for their own editor, that nobody so far has actually made a good editor to plug into that.
cues.zh: 所以那些习惯了所有 Vim 命令、积累了大量自写函数和脚本的人，在 Eclipse 里就用不了它们，这就成了个问题。Eclipse 的主要问题在于他们定义了一套编辑器接口，理论上你确实可以接入另一个编辑器。但那个接口太复杂了，实际上完全是为他们自己的编辑器量身定制的，所以至今还没人能做出一个好用的编辑器插件接入进去。

cues.en: There are a few solutions. Somebody has made an Eclipse Editor plugin. I've never tried it. I don't know. You're raising rent. You know how good it is? Yes, you were talking about Mosex for the video. I don't know how it works exactly. I do know that the KDE people have worked on this so that you could use the GVIM with the Qt stuff.
cues.zh: 目前有几种解决方案。有人做过一个 Eclipse 编辑器插件。我没试过，不太清楚。你举手了？你知道好不好用吗？对，你刚才提到了用于视频的 Mosex。我不太清楚它具体的运作方式。但我确实知道 KDE 团队一直在做这方面的工作，好让你能在 Qt 环境中使用 GVIM。

cues.en: and plug it in into basically any KDE application. But it had issues, mostly with keyboard focus and stuff like that. And somehow they have given up on that and started their own editor. So nobody's working on using Vim as a plugin. They're making a Vim a like editor for KDE. So unfortunately, that was a dead end, unless somebody picks it up. It would be really nice if we have a universal solution to that problem.
cues.zh: 然后把它接入几乎任何 KDE 应用。但它有问题，主要是键盘焦点之类的问题。后来不知怎么他们就放弃了，开始做自己的编辑器。所以现在没人在做把 Vim 作为插件的方案。他们在为 KDE 做一个类 Vim 编辑器。所以很不幸，那是一条死路，除非有人接手。如果这个问题能有一个通用方案，那就太好了。

cues.en: Ideally, you would have an editor interface that all applications use, but it doesn't exist. And I think it will be really, really difficult to convince everybody to use it. So yeah, hijacking a window, you can do that. But then how are you going to synchronize the text? How are you going to handle keyboard focus and stuff like that? OK, yeah, that's the out of window solution.
cues.zh: 理想情况下，会有一个所有应用都使用的编辑器接口，但它并不存在。而且我觉得要说服所有人用它，真的会非常非常难。所以，劫持窗口，你可以这么做。但之后你怎么同步文本？怎么处理键盘焦点之类的问题？好，对，那就是窗口外方案。

cues.en: Yeah, actually, I've tried using it, but somehow I didn't manage to set it up correctly to use Vim. Maybe that's a problem. But yeah, it's actually a variant of the copy-paste solution where you copy the text that's there into Vim, you edit it, and the moment you save it, it's automatically put back into the original text. It sounds very simple. I don't know why nobody has made it yet. Maybe an idea for someone? 20% project?
cues.zh: 对，其实我试过用它，但不知怎么没能正确配置好来使用 Vim。也许这就是个问题。不过对，它其实是复制粘贴方案的一个变种：你把那里的文本复制到 Vim，编辑它，一保存就会自动放回原文本。听起来很简单。我不知道为什么还没人做出来。也许可以给谁当个点子？20% 项目？

cues.en: I'm sorry, I didn't hear the first word. Yes, Microsoft Visual Studio, the older version actually had a possibility that you could add a few buttons inside. And if you click on them, then the text would appear in film. And you could send it back to Visual Studio. As far as I know, it doesn't work with the later versions of Visual Studio.
cues.zh: 抱歉，我没听清第一个词。对，Microsoft Visual Studio，旧版本其实可以让你在里面加几个按钮。点它们，文本就会出现在 Vim 里。然后你可以把它送回 Visual Studio。据我所知，它在较新版本的 Visual Studio 里不能用。

cues.en: And also, I don't know if somebody's working on it, but I've not heard of a solution. I think it must be possible, because I know some other companies, mostly commercial companies, actually do something like that. So I think it's possible. And again, it must have somebody who actually dives into the problem and solves it. At this moment, I'm mostly busy just with fixing the bugs and the existing features.
cues.zh: 另外，我不知道有没有人在做，但我没听说过有解决方案。我觉得一定可行，因为我知道其他一些公司，主要是商业公司，确实在做类似的事。所以我认为是可能的。而且，还是得有个人真正深入这个问题并解决它。目前我主要忙于修 bug 和处理现有功能。

cues.en: I don't really have time to work on new features, unless they're really small or quick to do. So I'm afraid that most of the feature requests are currently on hold, until I find some more time. Or somebody bright steps up and say, oh, I know how to do that. Actually, you know, actually, Jacobon was here. I can't pronounce his name properly. Jacobon Laxmanon. Do I say that right? OK.
cues.zh: 我真的没时间做新功能，除非它们非常小或者很快能做完。所以恐怕大多数功能请求目前都搁置着，直到我能找出更多时间。或者有聪明人站出来说，哦，我知道怎么做。其实，你知道，Jacobon 之前在这儿。我念不准他的名字。Jacobon Laxmanon。我念对了吗？好。

cues.en: And he's actually helping me now with some of the features that are on the to-do list. So that's really good. I really appreciate it. So I wish we had more people like that. OK, one more question. It depends. The mouse can be very productive. For example, if you take scrolling. Oh, we have a scroll bar here. Suppose I would like to move this scroll bar without using the mouse.
cues.zh: 而且他现在确实在帮我做一些待办清单上的功能。所以这真的很好。我非常感激。所以我希望能有更多这样的人。好，还有一个问题。看情况。鼠标可以非常高效。比如滚动。哦，我们这里有个滚动条。假设我想不用鼠标移动这个滚动条。

cues.en: Then I have to use control E or control D, something like that. And how do you say that? The connection between typing that and what you're seeing in the scrolling is not very direct. And it can be very slow. Well, if I just pick up the bubble of the scroll bar, that's so much more convenient. Of course, the problem is you have to pick up. So you can also use the scroll button. You can't see that.
cues.zh: 那我就得按 Ctrl+E 或 Ctrl+D 之类的。怎么说呢？敲键盘和屏幕滚动之间的反馈不够直接。而且可能非常慢。要是直接拖动滚动条的滑块，那就方便多了。当然，问题是你得伸手去拿鼠标。所以你也可以用滚轮。你们看不到这个。

cues.en: But I have a scroll button on this mouse. And quite often, that's very convenient for scrolling through. Now I am showing my famously. I wasn't supposed to do that. So yeah, sometimes the mouse is very convenient. So I think it's up to you. It's just that if you're using the mouse a lot, you have to think, isn't there a keyboard shortcut that's faster to do this? In VIM, of course, there is.
cues.zh: 但我这个鼠标上有个滚轮。很多时候，用它来翻页滚动特别方便。现在我都当众展示起来了，我本来不该这么干的。所以没错，有时候鼠标真的很方便。所以我觉得这取决于你自己。只是如果你频繁用鼠标，就该琢磨一下，是不是有更快的快捷键能搞定？在 Vim 里，当然是有的。

cues.en: In other applications, you often end up using the mouse. I mean, graphical applications are meant to be used with the mouse. That's very difficult to use keyboard shortcuts to move between fields in a form, for example. Then just a click, and it's so much easier. GFM is basically a graphical layer around the console theme. It's more like a very special kind of terminal.
cues.zh: 在其他应用里，你往往还是得用鼠标。我是说，图形界面应用本来就是设计给鼠标用的。比如在表单的各个输入框之间切换，用快捷键就很费劲。那时候点一下鼠标，就要轻松得多。GVim 基本上就是控制台版外面套了一层图形界面。它更像是一种非常特殊的终端。

cues.en: There's a few more connections to make it work better. But if I look at myself, I always use Vim in Exterm. Exterm supports the mouse. It supports coloring. It supports everything that I want to use. And it's so much more quick in doing things than starting G Vim. And then you have to grab the mouse to point to the right window, things like that.
cues.zh: 它加了一些连接处理让体验更好。但就我自己而言，我总是在 xterm 里用 Vim。xterm 支持鼠标，支持色彩，支持我想用的一切功能。而且比起启动 GVim，它运行起来要快得多。用 GVim 的话，你还得抓起鼠标去对准窗口之类的。

cues.en: And also, if you want to use external commands like grep or just use a copy command or whatever, that works better in a terminal than it does in GVIM. So for Vim, I would recommend using the console version in a good terminal. I mostly use extern because if there's something in extern I don't like, I just asked Thomas Dickey to change it. And that works. OK, another question?
cues.zh: 另外，如果你想用像 grep 这样的外部命令，或者单纯用个复制命令之类的，在终端里用也比在 GVim 里顺手。所以对于 Vim，我建议在一个好用的终端里使用控制台版本。我主要用 xterm，因为如果 xterm 里有我不喜欢的地方，我只要让 Thomas Dickey 改一下就行了，管用得很。好的，还有问题吗？

cues.en: No, you'll have to make that. OK, the question actually was, can we do completion based on Google Lookups? Yeah, some clever way of doing completion. Well, if you look into the completion methods, there's actually a function you can define to do your own kind of completion. And so you can use that basically to fetch the matches you want to find anywhere.
cues.zh: 没有，这个得你自己做。好，刚才的问题其实是：我们能不能基于 Google 搜索结果来做补全？是的，某种巧妙的补全方式。嗯，如果你去研究补全机制，其实可以自定义一个函数来实现你自己的补全方式。这样你基本上就能用它从任何地方获取你想匹配的内容。

cues.en: The only tricky thing is speed. Of course, if you want to use Google to look up some matches, I don't know how fast that will be, depending on your connection, how fast Google is, and stuff like that. But there are certainly possibilities there. I saw a question over there. What did I do right to make the winner among all competitors? I think the main thing was that I just kept working on it.
cues.zh: 唯一棘手的就是速度。当然，如果你想用 Google 检索匹配项，我不知道会有多快，这取决于你的网络连接、Google 的响应速度等等。但从技术上讲肯定是有可能的。我看到那边有个问题。我做对了什么才让 Vim 在所有竞争者中胜出？我觉得最主要的是，我一直坚持做下去了。

cues.en: All the others have disappeared. I know Elvis was very good, and I liked it a lot. There's some ideas that I didn't like, but overall it was good. But what's his name? The person making it. He actually decided at one point that he had to do a complete redesign of the source code. So then for two years, nothing happened except that he was working somewhere on the new version. Then when the new version appeared, it didn't do much more.
cues.zh: 其他那些都销声匿迹了。我知道 Elvis 曾非常优秀，我也很喜欢它。虽然有些设计理念我不太认同，但整体上很棒。但叫什么名字来着？那个作者。他后来决定必须把源码彻底重构一遍。于是整整两年毫无动静，就他自己在哪闷头做新版。后来新版终于出来了，功能上其实没多大长进。

cues.en: than the previous version. The source code was probably great, but nobody looks at that when you're using it. So that kind of was the end of Elvis. Stevie has not been worked on for a long time, haven't seen it. One of the other good competitors is NVI, new VI, which is actually the BSD reincarnation of the original VI. Kit Bossitz worked on that. He did a really fantastic job. I mean, I don't know how he did it.
cues.zh: 比起上一版来。源码可能确实很漂亮，但大家用的时候谁看源码呢。所以 Elvis 差不多就这么凉了。Stevie 也早就没人维护了，好久没见到了。另一个强劲的对手是 NVI，也就是 new VI，它其实是原版 VI 在 BSD 上的转世重构。Kit Bossitz 开发了它。他干得极其出色。我是说，我都不知道他是怎么做到的。

cues.en: Just under a year, he created a whole new editor that not only was completely VI compatible, because he really figured out every little bug that VI did that you could call a feature. And he reproduced it in NVI. And he also added a lot of new things, like multi-windows, multi-buffers, multi-level undo, and all kinds of fancy things. So that was great.
cues.zh: 前后不到一年，他就写出了一个全新的编辑器，不仅完全兼容 VI——因为他把原版 VI 里所有被当作特性的小 bug 都摸得一清二楚。还在 NVI 里把它们原样复现了。而且他还加了好多新特性，比如多窗口、多缓冲区、多级撤销，以及各种炫酷的功能。真的非常了不起。

cues.en: And actually, at that moment, when he introduced it, I was thinking, well, I might as well stop working on film, because that one's better. But I didn't. I actually added windows and buffers and stuff to film. So I can still compete with that one. But the same thing happened. Keith just stopped working on it. If he would have continued, I think NVI would have been much, much better. But he didn't work on it. So now you are stuck with him.
cues.zh: 实际上在那个时候，他发布出来之后，我心想，算了吧，不如放弃继续搞 Vim 了，因为人家那个更好。但我没放弃。我给 Vim 也加上了窗口、缓冲区等特性。这样我就还能跟它竞争。但同样的事又发生了。Keith 后来也不再维护了。如果他继续搞下去，我认为 NVI 会强大得多得多。但他没再做下去。所以现在你们就只能凑合着用 Vim 了。

cues.en: OK, one more question. Actually, the FIM license is GPL compatible, but it's not GPL. You want to know why? Does GPL software survive longer than non-GPL software? I don't think so, because the license doesn't really change your software. But there's a twist there. Using a GPL license sometimes means it's GNU software.
cues.zh: 好，再回答一个问题。实际上，Vim 的许可证兼容 GPL，但它并不是 GPL。你想知道为什么？GPL 软件会比非 GPL 软件活得更久吗？我不这么认为，因为许可证并不会真正改变你的软件。但这里有个微妙之处。使用 GPL 许可证有时意味着它是 GNU 软件。

cues.en: So part of the GNU project. And that means there's like a big crop of people that will take over the maintenance when the original author disappears or just gives up. And I don't know exactly how to do it, but they have some kind of system to keep things going. But that's different from the license. GPL is a license and GNU is a project. So it's not the same thing. Although I think every project in GNU has to use the GPL. I think so. I'm not sure, actually.
cues.zh: 也就是 GNU 项目的一部分。这就意味着有一大群人，会在原作者消失或放弃维护时接手过来。我不太清楚他们具体怎么运作的，但他们确实有一套机制来保持项目运转。但这跟许可证是两码事。GPL 是许可证，而 GNU 是项目。两者不是一回事。虽然我觉得 GNU 里的每个项目都必须使用 GPL。好像是这样。其实我也说不准。

cues.en: Yeah, the license for VIM, I wrote that a long time ago when I thought, well, let's just make some kind of license. And nobody was actually actively discussing about licenses at that time. So I just made one that I thought was nice. Just give it away. But you can actually change it, but you have to give the changes to me. So I can decide if I want to include them or not. Very basic. But over time, you have to add certain exceptions because people think, hey, but if I do this, then your license doesn't cover it. OK, I'll change it.
cues.zh: 对，Vim 的许可证是我很久以前写的，当时我就想，随便搞个许可证吧。那时其实也没什么人热烈讨论许可证这回事。所以我就写了一个自认为还不错的。就是白送给大家。但你也可以修改它，只不过得把修改发给我。这样我好决定要不要合进去。非常简单粗暴。但随着时间推移，你不得不加上一些例外条款，因为有人会觉得，嘿，要是我这么干，你的许可证就没覆盖到这种情况。行吧，那我就改改。

cues.en: At one point of time, some people found out that people compiled Vim with a GPL library. I think it was the mouse library that's used on the Linux console. That's actually a GPL library, not LGPL, but GPL. And then if you compile Vim like that, you can't give it to somebody else, because the Vim license was incompatible with GPL. If you compile it with a GPL library, you can't pass it on to anybody. So then people asked me to make the license GPL compatible.
cues.zh: 有一段时间，有人发现大家会用 GPL 库来编译 Vim。我记得是 Linux 控制台上用的鼠标库。那个库其实是 GPL 库，不是 LGPL，而是 GPL。那样编译 Vim 的话，你就不能把它交给别人，因为 Vim 许可证与 GPL 不兼容。如果你用 GPL 库编译它，就不能把它传给任何人。于是人们让我把许可证改成与 GPL 兼容。

cues.en: And I did that. And actually, Richard Stallman himself looked into the license and gave me a few hints until he was satisfied with it. Went in a very nice way. So no complaints about it. So now the FIM license is GPL compatible. As far as I know, I mean, we don't hire lawyers to do this. So we just have a fresh look at it and think, well, it should be OK. And I've never had the license problem, so don't worry about it.
cues.zh: 我照做了。其实 Richard Stallman 本人也看过这个许可证，还给了一些提示，直到他满意为止。过程非常顺利，所以没什么可抱怨的。现在 Vim 许可证已经与 GPL 兼容了。据我所知——我的意思是，我们不会雇律师来做这件事。我们只是重新看一遍，然后想，嗯，应该没问题。我从来没遇到过许可证问题，所以不用担心。

cues.en: You can use Vim, you can use the source code, and just be happy with it. Let's take one or two more questions. In the very back there. And what? Oh, GDB. Is there other plans to integrate Vim and GDB? Actually, that's been done. It's called Aghida. And that was actually a project I worked on a few years ago. Yeah, the problem is.
cues.zh: 你可以用 Vim，也可以用它的源代码，开心用就好。我们再接一两个问题。最后面那位。什么？哦，GDB。还有别的把 Vim 和 GDB 集成的计划吗？其实已经做过了。它叫 Aghida。那其实是我几年前参与的一个项目。对，问题是……

cues.en: The remark is that it's difficult to install. The problem is it uses WX Python, and that's a nice graphical library. It really has a nice interface, but it can be difficult to install. It's like a hit and miss. Sometimes it works, but then they make some changes in GTK or some of the lower layers, and then it doesn't work. Then they fix it, and it works again.
cues.zh: 有人提到它很难安装。问题在于它用的是 wxPython，那是个不错的图形库。它的界面确实很好，但可能很难安装。有点像碰运气。有时能用，但后来他们在 GTK 或某些底层做了改动，它就不能用了。然后他们修好，它又能用了。

cues.en: Actually, the last time I upgraded my OS, it worked properly, so I can run it. But yeah, it's tricky. And also, I made that as a start, as an example of how it could work. And to explain a little bit more about it, it's a Python application that is a connection between GDB and Vim. So it runs GDB, it runs Vim, and then connects the two. So if you, in GDB, list.
cues.zh: 其实我上次升级操作系统时，它能正常工作，所以我可以运行它。不过是的，这有点麻烦。另外，我做它只是作为一个起点，一个展示它可以如何工作的例子。再稍微解释一下，它是一个 Python 应用，用来连接 GDB 和 Vim。它会运行 GDB，运行 Vim，然后把两者连接起来。所以如果你在 GDB 里列出……

cues.en: the source code, it will show in Vim. And in Vim, you can set a breakpoint, and that breakpoint goes back to GDB. And actually, what I did is I just added enough so I could use it. And I actually use it to debug Vim. But the problem is I made it myself, so I know how it works. And for other people, they probably use different commands and say, oh, it doesn't do what I like. And they give up and throw it away. And so it exists.
cues.zh: 源代码，它就会显示在 Vim 里。而在 Vim 里，你可以设置断点，这个断点会传回 GDB。其实我做的就是加上了足够的功能，让我自己能用的程度。我确实用它来调试 Vim。但问题是我自己做的，所以我知道它怎么工作。对其他人来说，他们可能会用不同的命令，然后说，哦，它做不到我想要的。然后他们就放弃并把它扔掉了。所以它确实存在。

cues.en: It could do with a little bit of work. So if somebody's interested, it's all on the web. It's all in downloads. It's actually, well, we don't need it. I actually have a screen safe that picks a random one, so I was wondering if it would pick some of my pictures. Anyway, the name is Aghida. Maybe I can look it up. Let's see. No, that's wrong. Sorry. Let's take a new window. OK, that's how it's spelled.
cues.zh: 它还可以再改进一点。所以如果有人感兴趣，它都在网上，都在下载区。其实，嗯，我们不需要它。我有个屏幕保护程序会随机选一张，所以我在想它会不会选到我的某些照片。总之，名字是 Aghida。也许我可以查一下。看看。不，那不对。抱歉。我们开个新窗口。好，这才是正确的拼写。

cues.en: And it doesn't work because I'm not connected. I'm not sure if this works. Let's try. I don't think so. Anyway, you can see how it works. I don't quite get the question. You have lots of options, of course, yeah? Oh, to donate. Oh, that's a good question. Thanks for asking. Well, actually, when I was working on VIM7, you may have noticed that at that time, I quit my job, basically.
cues.zh: 这行不通，因为我没连上网。我不确定这个能不能用。试试看。我觉得不行。总之，你们能看到它是怎么运作的。我不太明白这个问题。当然，你有很多选择，对吧？哦，是问捐款。哦，这个问题问得好。谢谢提问。其实，当我开发 VIM7 时，你可能注意到了，那时我基本上辞掉了工作。

cues.en: And I started working on VIM full time. So at that time, I asked people to please give me some money to survive. And that worked quite well. And I survived. But then VIM 7 was ready. And I thought, well, let's get a real job again. So I decided to work for Google. And at that moment, I thought, well, I don't need that money anymore. But people kept sending it. So that money is actually now all.
cues.zh: 我开始全职开发 Vim。所以那时，我请大家给我一些钱来维持生活。效果挺好。我活下来了。但后来 VIM 7 完成了。我想，好吧，再找份正经工作吧。于是我决定去 Google 工作。那时我想，好吧，我不需要那笔钱了。但人们还在继续寄钱。所以那笔钱现在其实全都

cues.en: going to the same Uganda project that I've always been talking about as Charityware for Vim. So that kind of doubled the donations that are going to Uganda. So that's very good. And people just keep donating to Vim. I think most people do that as a sort of a thank you for this nice editor that they're using the whole day. And they think, well, I would like to give something back. And OK, give me some money, and I'll give it to the needy children in Uganda.
cues.zh: 捐给我一直提到的同一个 Uganda 项目，作为 Vim 的 Charityware。这差不多让捐给 Uganda 的款项翻了一倍。这非常好。人们一直在给 Vim 捐款。我觉得大多数人这么做，是为了感谢这个他们整天都在用的好编辑器。他们想，好吧，我想回馈点什么。那好，给我一些钱，我会把它交给 Uganda 的贫困儿童。

cues.en: And they can really need that money. I should show you at least what I'm talking about. Oh, that's not what I wanted. Actually, this is the right website with the wrong page. But this is actually, if you're interested in the books I was talking about, the highly effective people book by Stephen Covey, and the highly defective people book by, what's his name, the writer of Dilbert. And if you want to buy them.
cues.zh: 他们真的很需要那笔钱。我至少该给你们看看我在说什么。哦，这不是我想打开的。其实，网站是对的，页面不对。不过这里其实——如果你对我说的书感兴趣，Stephen Covey 的《高效能人士的七个习惯》，还有那本《高效能缺陷人士》，作者叫什么来着，Dilbert 的作者。如果你想买它们的话。

cues.en: I can recommend them. They're really nice books. And they're not that expensive. If you use this web page and click on the links and order them from Amazon, and there's actually several Amazon places where you can get them. So if you're not in the US, but somewhere else, in Canada, or UK, or Germany, you can use one of the links. Then actually a percentage of the sales also goes to the children in Uganda. So it doesn't cost you anything extra.
cues.zh: 我可以推荐它们。它们真是好书。而且不算贵。如果你用这个网页，点击链接，从 Amazon 订购，其实有几个 Amazon 站点都能买到。所以如果你不在美国，而是在别的地方，比如加拿大、英国或德国，你可以用其中一个链接。这样销售的一部分也会捐给 Uganda 的儿童。所以你不会多花任何钱。

cues.en: What can I say about the project? Well, this is not really a talk about the project itself. So I'll just mention it. There's a website here with information and a nice picture. There's more pictures. Basically, I've always been trying to promote this project in Uganda. That's very good to help the children there. Most of them are orphans. They really need our help.
cues.zh: 关于这个项目我能说什么呢？其实，这不是一个专门讲项目本身的演讲。所以我只提一下。这里有个网站，有信息和一张好看的照片。还有更多照片。基本上，我一直都在努力推广 Uganda 的这个项目。这对帮助那里的孩子很有好处。他们大多数是孤儿。他们真的需要我们的帮助。

cues.en: The project concentrates around education. These people are poor. You would think, well, just feed them, and that's it. Now we want to educate them, so that eventually, hopefully after several years, they can take care of themselves. That's the goal of the project. But we're not there yet. It's going to take a long time. We have a big school. We have about 700 children in school. Every year, about 20 to 50 children finish school, and hopefully they will do something useful.
cues.zh: 这个项目集中在教育上。这些人很穷。你可能会想，好吧，给他们吃的就行了。现在我们要教育他们，这样最终，希望几年之后，他们能自己照顾自己。这就是项目的目标。但我们还没做到。这需要很长时间。我们有一所规模很大的学校。学校里有大约 700 个孩子。每年大约有 20 到 50 个孩子毕业，希望他们能做些有用的事。

cues.en: And we already see some of the students coming back to the center as a teacher or as a help in the clinic. And we can see it starting to run itself. And that's very promising. But we're not there yet. We need a lot of money to keep it running. So if you feel you need to give something to someone, think about this one.
cues.zh: 我们已经看到一些学生回到中心当老师，或者在诊所里帮忙。可以看到它已经开始自运转了。这前景非常好。但我们还没完全做到那一步。维持运转还需要很多资金。所以如果你想捐助某个项目，可以考虑这一个。

cues.en: I think we're going too far off track here, because it's totally unrelated to film. So maybe we can talk about this afterwards. I'll hang around so we can talk about it. But I've been there for more than a year, so that's good. I know quite a few things about the project, so that's why I can recommend it, and not all the other ones. There's many of them, but this one is really good. OK, that's a very short summary. OK, maybe one or two more questions.
cues.zh: 我觉得我们扯得有点太远了，因为这跟 Vim 完全没关系。所以也许我们可以会后再聊。我会留在这儿，到时候可以交流。不过我在那待了一年多，挺好的。我对这个项目了解不少，所以才会推荐它，而不是别的项目。同类项目很多，但这一个真的很棒。好了，简短总结就到这里。行，也许再答一两个问题。

cues.en: OK, there's one. Using tabs effectively. Yeah, of course, you can use lots of windows, as many as you like. It mostly depends on your screen size, actually. If you have a big screen, you can use lots of windows. If you have a small screen, like this small laptop that I'm using, you can't really fit more than two windows on there without having the problem that you have to scroll a lot. I think that's the main problem if your windows get
cues.zh: 好，这儿有一个。如何高效使用标签页。当然，你可以开很多窗口，想开多少开多少。其实这主要取决于你的屏幕尺寸。如果你屏幕很大，可以开很多窗口。如果是小屏幕，比如我现在用的这台小笔记本，开两个以上的窗口就会遇到必须频繁滚动的问题。我认为主要问题在于如果窗口变得

cues.en: too small, you have to scroll a lot to see where you are. And for me, what I'm mostly doing, I start multiple x-terms, like four or even more. And it's very easy to switch between x-terms. So inside Vim, I don't use many windows, mostly too maximum. And then if I need to work on something else, I just go to another x-terms, start Vim there, and continue. And of course, you can copy, paste file names and marks and whatever.
cues.zh: 太小，你就得不停滚动才能看清当前位置。对我来说，我平时的做法是启动多个 xterm，比如四个甚至更多。在不同 xterm 之间切换非常容易。所以在 Vim 内部我不太用很多窗口，最多也就两个。如果需要处理别的事情，我就切到另一个 xterm，在那里启动 Vim 继续干活。当然，文件名、标记之类的也可以随意复制粘贴。

cues.en: That works good for me. Tap pages, they're very nice. And you can actually have multiple windows on one tap page. So it's like you have multiple VIM sessions just next to each other. Organize them as you like. I don't really use them myself very much, but that's probably mainly because I'm an all-time VIM user, and they weren't there, so I have the habit of doing it one way. And now we have tap pages.
cues.zh: 这种方式对我挺合适。标签页功能很棒，你甚至可以在一个标签页里放多个窗口。这就好比多个 Vim 会话并排放在一起，随你组织。我自己其实不太常用，主要是因为我是 Vim 的老用户了，以前没有这个功能，所以习惯了固定的工作流。现在虽然有了标签页，

cues.en: I don't really need them. So obviously, you can sort of sort your work in different tab pages, especially if you don't have an x-term, but you have to use GFIM, for example, on Windows. Then they're very useful, because you don't want to start many copies of GFIM there, perhaps. Depends on what you're doing.
cues.zh: 我倒不是真的很需要。显然，你可以把工作划分到不同的标签页里，尤其是没有 xterm 的时候，比如在 Windows 上用 gVim。那时候标签页就非常管用了，因为你可能不想在 Windows 上开一堆 gVim 实例。这也取决于你在做什么。

cues.en: And of course, it's a quick way to switch between different pages with Windows. And so if you organize them in different work groups or different things you're working on, you have to be careful not to get too many of them. If you have like 20 different tab pages, you're probably doing something wrong. That's not the right way to do that. There's other ways to organize lots of files. OK, does it answer your question? Hopefully. I think I'll take one more question and then we
cues.zh: 当然，这也是在带有多个窗口的不同标签页之间快速切换的方法。如果你按不同的工作组或任务来组织它们，得注意别开太多。如果你开了二十来个标签页，可能用法就不太对了。那不是正确的使用姿势，组织大量文件还有其他办法。好，解答你的问题了吗？希望如此。我想再接一个问题，然后我们

cues.en: can just socialize. OK, final question. Who's up for it? How to use the VIM info? Well, if you talk about sessions or VIM info, those are two different things. VIM info just stores the last information of the last VIM you exited, because that's when it stores it automatically. You can also store it manually. At one point in time, you can say, OK, store what I have now in my VIM info file, or even create another VIM info file.
cues.zh: 就可以自由交流了。好，最后一个问题，谁来？怎么使用 viminfo？嗯，会话（sessions）和 viminfo 是两码事。viminfo 只保存你最后退出的那个 Vim 的信息，因为那是它自动保存的时机。你也可以手动保存，在某个时间点把当前状态保存到 viminfo 文件中，甚至新建另一个 viminfo 文件。

cues.en: But that's not very comfortable. If you talk about sessions, like what we were talking about, a session with multiple windows. So you're working on some project, and you have multiple source file that you're working on. You say, OK, now I have to go home. I want to start this again tomorrow. The best thing to do is then to make a session from it with the make session, mk session command. You can store it somewhere, and you recall it later.
cues.zh: 但那样用起来不太顺手。说到会话，就像我们刚才聊到的多窗口会话。假设你正在做某个项目，同时在写好几个源文件。你说，好了，我现在得回家了，明天还想接着写。这时最好的办法就是用 make session，也就是 mksession 命令生成一个会话。你可以把它存下来，之后再随时恢复。

cues.en: You can also use it to store views on a file with all your option settings and stuff. But I think the main thing is store a session as a session under a name, and you can reload it. It doesn't store everything. There's actually an option that specifies what you can store in your session, and that you can switch on and off. The default is pretty good, I think. But again, it depends on what you're doing. The film info is completely automatic.
cues.zh: 你也可以用它来保存某个文件的视图，包括所有选项设置之类的。但我认为最核心的还是给会话起个名字保存下来，之后可以重新加载。它并不会保存所有东西。其实有个选项可以指定会话中保存的内容，你可以自由开关。我觉得默认设置就很不错了。不过这还是取决于你的具体需求。而 viminfo 则是完全自动的。

cues.en: I use it an awful lot. For example, if you edit a file, you exit Vim, you open it again, and you type colon e, and just use going back in the command line history, you find what's been stored in the Vim info file. Same for search patterns, marks, and stuff like that. Quite often, you don't really think ahead and think, I have to get back here. So you don't remember to put a mark there.
cues.zh: 我平时用得非常多。比如你编辑完一个文件退出 Vim，再次打开后输入冒号 e，只需翻一下命令行历史记录，就能找到 viminfo 文件里保存的内容。搜索模式、标记（marks）之类的也是同理。很多时候你事先并不会想到“我待会儿还得回到这里”，所以压根不会记得随手打个标记。

cues.en: You just exit Vim, and then a few hours later you think, oh, I have to go back there. And where was I? And then the numbered marks are very useful. So you can use quote one, quote two, quote three, and you go back to all the positions where you exited Vim the last nine times. So that's not really a session, but in Vim info file. OK, I think that's it.
cues.zh: 你就直接退出了 Vim，几个小时后才想起：“哎呀，我还得回那里去，我刚才写到哪儿来着？”这时数字标记就非常管用了。你可以用单引号 1、单引号 2、单引号 3，跳回过去九次退出 Vim 时的位置。所以这其实不属于会话，而是记录在 viminfo 文件里的。好了，差不多就是这些。

cues.en: Thank you very much for coming. I'm so happy that so many of you showed up. I really enjoyed talking to you.
cues.zh: 非常感谢大家的到来。很高兴看到这么多人到场。今天和大家交流非常开心。
